chapter: Rockwell: playing with the Lewis band
title: Frank Rockwell's route to the Lewis band
summary: Banjoist Rockwell says he listened to the Lewis band before sitting in at the Beverly Cavern, and describes his earlier bands.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What were the circumstances which led to your playing with the George Lewis band?

I had been an avid listener at that time and previously I had been interested in various forms of Dixieland jazz and then I got interested in the Lewis band prior to the time they were out and then the various times they would come out I would be a listener and I talked to them but it's not overly intimate. He had already left. I remember I was drafted in the last one. It was an arrangement for dear to dear 21. Yeah.
Okay, well, how'd you have any previous experience playing with any other band?

When I was 17 or 18, I walked into the Beverly Caverns, the same place. On Monday night, they held it jam session night, which normally just the regular band played. I just walked in one night with my banjo, and it was the Turk Murphy band at that time, and they let me play, and the Pat Pat and the banjo player at that time set out a set, and they let me play the whole night. And there were a lot of tunes I didn't know, but I was able to listen and hear the chords, and a lot of minors and strange keys, you know.
But had you not played with any sort of other band on the West Coast on any regular basses?

I played with a high school band where we played on television and things like that, and won wristwatches, and I played it. Now, in 1954, I started a band called the Storyville Stompers in college. Let's see, in the 54, I guess so, but just various little jobs, you know, nothing of any importance.
